world.title: Tajikistan starts one-year withdrawal from International Criminal Court
world.summary: Tajikistan notified the United Nations on Nov. 20 that it is withdrawing from the Rome Statute, beginning a one-year process to leave the International Criminal Court (ICC), the permanent tribunal that prosecutes individuals for the gravest international crimes. The notice came on the day Russian President Vladimir Put
world.content: Tajikistan notified the United Nations on Nov. 20 that it is withdrawing from the Rome Statute, beginning a one-year process to leave the International Criminal Court (ICC), the permanent tribunal that prosecutes individuals for the gravest international crimes. The notice came on the day Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Tajikistan; the ICC issued an arrest warrant for him in 2023 over the alleged unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children. Tajikistan’s lower house of parliament approved a withdrawal resolution on Oct. 1. The country is the fourth to begin withdrawing since the United States called in July for countries to leave the court. The ICC’s governing body and the European Union criticized the decision. Tajikistan’s withdrawal will take effect one year after notification, but it will not erase obligations incurred while the country was a member.
world.image_alt: Tajikistan starts one-year withdrawal from International Criminal Court

world.title: Exiled Sheikh Hasina seeks Bangladesh return as Dhaka vows arrest
world.summary: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return from India on Dec. 16, Victory Day, and has asked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government to arrange a flight from Delhi on the national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Her spokesperson says the government has a constitutional responsibilit
world.content: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return from India on Dec. 16, Victory Day, and has asked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government to arrange a flight from Delhi on the national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Her spokesperson says the government has a constitutional responsibility to bring her back; Dhaka says she can return only through extradition and would be arrested. No flight arrangements have been agreed, and India has not publicly responded to the latest request. Hasina fled to India on Aug. 5, 2024, after a student-led uprising ended her 15-year rule. Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal sentenced her to death in absentia in November 2025 over the crackdown on the protests; she denies the charges. The United Nations has estimated that as many as 1,400 people died during the unrest. Her Awami League party is banned, and supporters have held protests demanding her return. Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, while the chief prosecutor in Hasina’s case questioned why the government should arrange transport for someone convicted in absentia. India said in April it was examining Bangladesh’s extradition request. Hasina’s proposed return date is Dec. 16, but her travel arrangements and legal status remain unresolved.
world.image_alt: Exiled Sheikh Hasina seeks Bangladesh return as Dhaka vows arrest

world.title: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher over unauthorized nude photos
world.summary: Gisèle Pelicot said she would take legal action against French publisher Tinbad and psychoanalyst Sabine Prokhoris after nude photographs of her were used without her consent to promote Prokhoris’ essay on coercive control. The images, taken by her former husband, were sent to some media outlets to publicize the book.
world.content: Gisèle Pelicot said she would take legal action against French publisher Tinbad and psychoanalyst Sabine Prokhoris after nude photographs of her were used without her consent to promote Prokhoris’ essay on coercive control. The images, taken by her former husband, were sent to some media outlets to publicize the book. Pelicot said she was “deeply shocked” and refused to let her private life become an advertising tool. Tinbad apologized for what it called an “unfortunate communication error” and said it had not sent images of rape or pornographic videos. It did not deny distributing nude photographs. Prokhoris said the publisher bore full responsibility for the campaign and described her book as a critical examination of psychological control, not a study of the Pelicot case. The essay includes a chapter on the case, and its back-cover text describes coercive control as a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy. Tinbad said it would stop promoting the book and print no additional copies beyond the 280 already in circulation. Pelicot’s lawyer, Christophe Bigot, said the book challenges her status as a victim.
world.image_alt: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher over unauthorized nude photos

world.title: China names Pakistani astronaut for first foreign Tiangong mission
world.summary: China named Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Shenzhou-24 crew for a launch scheduled at 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Wednesday, Nov. 25, from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. Ali will be the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s Tiangong space station and the first non-Chinese member of a joint
world.content: China named Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Shenzhou-24 crew for a launch scheduled at 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Wednesday, Nov. 25, from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. Ali will be the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s Tiangong space station and the first non-Chinese member of a joint crew in China’s crewed space program. Ali will spend about a week aboard Tiangong before returning to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23 with two departing crew members. Chinese astronaut Zhu Yangzhu will stay aboard Tiangong for a year, twice the usual six-month rotation, to gather data on long-duration spaceflight. Ali’s participation follows a China-Pakistan space cooperation agreement signed in February 2025. China says it aims to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, while NASA has set a 2028 lunar landing target. The Shenzhou-24 launch will also begin the next crew rotation at Tiangong, where the incoming crew is expected to conduct research and routine maintenance.
world.image_alt: China names Pakistani astronaut for first foreign Tiangong mission

world.title: Pope Francis’ posthumous diary details spiritual crisis and struggles with power
world.summary: A book of excerpts from Pope Francis’ private diary, published Tuesday, recounts what he described as three encounters with the devil and a vision of the “gates of hell,” as well as a two-year spiritual crisis over power and governance. The journal spans 1992 to Aug. 18, 2024. Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, head of
world.content: A book of excerpts from Pope Francis’ private diary, published Tuesday, recounts what he described as three encounters with the devil and a vision of the “gates of hell,” as well as a two-year spiritual crisis over power and governance. The journal spans 1992 to Aug. 18, 2024. Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, head of the Vatican’s doctrine office, compiled and annotated the volume. Francis wrote that his 2021-22 crisis involved pressure over decisions, spiritual desolation and the temptation to believe he could solve everything. Fernández says Francis understood the crisis as a struggle against exercising power over others. The diary also records Francis’ regret that he had initially dismissed abuse victims’ claims in Chile before commissioning an investigation. Fernández says he left out entries affecting third parties. Francis’ most confidential notes, written in an indecipherable code, also do not appear in the book. The book is being released globally in several languages, with the Vatican’s publishing house publishing the Italian edition.
world.image_alt: Pope Francis’ posthumous diary details spiritual crisis and struggles with power

world.title: EU proposes sanctions on Russian banks, ex-combatants and sports
world.summary: The European Commission on Nov. 23 proposed the European Union’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia. It targets about 60 banks with transaction restrictions and removal from the SWIFT financial messaging network, as well as cryptocurrency and payment channels and more than 70 vessels linked to Russia’s shadow fleet.
world.content: The European Commission on Nov. 23 proposed the European Union’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia. It targets about 60 banks with transaction restrictions and removal from the SWIFT financial messaging network, as well as cryptocurrency and payment channels and more than 70 vessels linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. The plan would also bar European companies from building, operating or repairing Russian energy infrastructure, including electricity services, and prohibit EU citizens from holding leadership posts in Russian companies. The proposal would deny entry to Russians who fought in the war against Ukraine and bar Russian teams and athletes from competing under their national flag at EU events. It also targets Russian symbols at sporting events, sponsorship of European sports and cultural groups, and Russian nationals’ leadership roles in European sports federations. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the measures aim to increase pressure on Moscow and cited security concerns about former combatants. The package requires unanimous approval from all 27 EU member states, and Brussels is seeking agreement in December. Separately, the Commission has issued stricter guidance for tourist visas, including tighter checks and rejection of Russian passports without biometric features.
world.image_alt: EU proposes sanctions on Russian banks, ex-combatants and sports

world.title: Mexico will try cartel figure despite U.S. extradition request
world.summary: Mexico will prosecute Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, the alleged cartel leader known as “El Chapo Isidro,” despite a U.S. request to extradite him, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said Monday. Mexican forces captured him in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Nov. 20. Authorities said U.S. intelligence and surveillance drone flights hel
world.content: Mexico will prosecute Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, the alleged cartel leader known as “El Chapo Isidro,” despite a U.S. request to extradite him, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said Monday. Mexican forces captured him in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Nov. 20. Authorities said U.S. intelligence and surveillance drone flights helped locate him, but U.S. personnel did not take part on the ground. The raid and ensuing clashes left four Mexican soldiers and 16 suspected cartel members dead. Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said Mexico and the United States had shared intelligence for three months before the operation, which targeted a leader allied with the Los Mayos faction in Sinaloa’s ongoing cartel conflict. Mexico has charged Meza Flores with weapons offenses and possessing methamphetamine for sale. U.S. prosecutors accuse him of leading a cross-border drug network and have filed six charges. The capture led to further arrests, while experts warn that removing cartel leaders can prompt violent succession fights rather than dismantle their organizations.
world.image_alt: Mexico will try cartel figure despite U.S. extradition request

world.title: US blacklists Singapore-based Megaspeed over suspected Nvidia chip diversions
world.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department added Singapore-based cloud and data-center operator Megaspeed and six related companies in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List, requiring government licenses for shipments of U.S.-regulated goods and technology. The department cited a significant risk that the companies cou
world.content: The U.S. Commerce Department added Singapore-based cloud and data-center operator Megaspeed and six related companies in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List, requiring government licenses for shipments of U.S.-regulated goods and technology. The department cited a significant risk that the companies could divert advanced computing products to unauthorized users or uses; license applications face a presumption of denial. The listing also includes Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore subsidiary of Chinese technology company Alibaba. U.S. authorities have investigated Megaspeed since 2024 over allegations that it helped route Nvidia AI chips to China in breach of export controls. The Justice Department is conducting a criminal investigation. Beijing has denied separate U.S. intelligence allegations that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang acted for China; Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. Commerce announced the action on the same day Nvidia’s board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, who had resigned less than two weeks earlier. The decision followed public pressure from U.S. officials and lawmakers over why Commerce had not acted sooner. Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said his government is investigating possible breaches of Singapore law and coordinating with U.S. authorities; Malaysia has told data-center operators not to host or provide services to the listed firms.
world.image_alt: US blacklists Singapore-based Megaspeed over suspected Nvidia chip diversions

business.title: Experts warn holiday shoppers about fake deals and delivery scams
business.summary: Consumer-protection and financial experts are warning shoppers to watch for fake retail websites, misleading discounts and delivery scams during Black Friday and holiday shopping. More than a third of U.S. adults said they had received no refund for an online purchase that never arrived or turned out to be fake, accord
business.content: Consumer-protection and financial experts are warning shoppers to watch for fake retail websites, misleading discounts and delivery scams during Black Friday and holiday shopping. More than a third of U.S. adults said they had received no refund for an online purchase that never arrived or turned out to be fake, according to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey. Scammers exploit the rush of orders by posing as delivery companies and claiming a parcel needs an address correction or a small fee; fraudulent links can then harvest card details, passwords or banking approval codes. Consumer advisers recommend checking prices and terms carefully and not letting countdowns or limited-time offers rush a purchase. A financial adviser also urged online shoppers to visit retailers’ websites directly rather than follow unexpected links.
business.image_alt: Experts warn holiday shoppers about fake deals and delivery scams

business.title: New York Fed chief signals further rate hikes as inflation stays high
business.summary: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said the U.S. central bank must keep acting to bring inflation back to its 2% goal, signaling support for another increase at the Dec. 8-9 policy meeting. He said the pace of later moves would depend on incoming data. The Fed’s benchmark rate stands at 3.75%-4%, and mark
business.content: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said the U.S. central bank must keep acting to bring inflation back to its 2% goal, signaling support for another increase at the Dec. 8-9 policy meeting. He said the pace of later moves would depend on incoming data. The Fed’s benchmark rate stands at 3.75%-4%, and markets broadly expect a quarter-point increase next month. Williams expects inflation to end 2026 at 3.5%, ease to just above 2% next year and reach the target in 2028. He said the economy should grow 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027. He cited elevated energy prices as a source of inflation pressure but said pressures from tariffs, geopolitical conflict and demand related to artificial intelligence had not yet developed into significant, persistent inflation across the economy.
business.image_alt: New York Fed chief signals further rate hikes as inflation stays high

business.title: Anthropic raises $81 billion in Nasdaq IPO
business.summary: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in its November 19 Nasdaq listing, valuing it at $1.5 trillion. Shares were priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 after reaching $115.10; they closed at $88.91 on the second trading day. The company has yet to turn a profit, and
business.content: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in its November 19 Nasdaq listing, valuing it at $1.5 trillion. Shares were priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 after reaching $115.10; they closed at $88.91 on the second trading day. The company has yet to turn a profit, and its filings disclose $6.2 billion in debt and nearly $1 trillion in planned spending on chips and AI infrastructure through 2045. IPO expert Jay Ritter said the market was pricing in “very lofty expectations”.

business.title: Gold futures in India rebound 2.5% after 14-month low
business.summary: Gold futures in India rose about 2.4% on Monday, Nov. 23, recovering from a 14-month low reached the previous week. December-delivery contracts on the Multi Commodity Exchange gained 2,899 rupees to 124,677 rupees per 10 grams; a later intraday report put the contract up 2.53% at 124,857 rupees. The gains followed fres
business.content: Gold futures in India rose about 2.4% on Monday, Nov. 23, recovering from a 14-month low reached the previous week. December-delivery contracts on the Multi Commodity Exchange gained 2,899 rupees to 124,677 rupees per 10 grams; a later intraday report put the contract up 2.53% at 124,857 rupees. The gains followed fresh speculative positions and firm spot demand, The Indian Express reported. Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said technology-stock losses and weaker economic expectations tied to the AI boom led markets to reassess the US interest-rate outlook, supporting gold. CNBC reported spot gold at $3,657.14 an ounce at 9 a.m. ET Monday, compared with $3,571.30 at the same time Friday. Jewellery prices can exceed quoted gold rates because they can include making charges and goods and services tax.
business.image_alt: Gold futures in India rebound 2.5% after 14-month low

business.title: Compass plans to move primary listing from London to US
business.summary: Compass Group, the UK-based catering company, plans to move its primary stock-market listing from London to the United States, with an announcement expected alongside its full-year results on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Any move would require shareholder approval. The company is expected to retain a secondary London listing, and
business.content: Compass Group, the UK-based catering company, plans to move its primary stock-market listing from London to the United States, with an announcement expected alongside its full-year results on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Any move would require shareholder approval. The company is expected to retain a secondary London listing, and investor consultation could take more than a year. North America accounts for about two-thirds of Compass’s $46.1 billion in annual revenue and roughly three-quarters of its profit; 40% of its investors are based in the United States, a person close to the company told the Financial Times. Other companies have moved their main listings to the US, while London has recorded few new flotations.
business.image_alt: Compass plans to move primary listing from London to US

business.title: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok sexualized images
business.summary: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX and related companies on Nov. 23, alleging that Grok’s AI image tools enabled users to create sexualized images of real people, including children, and that the company misled consumers about safety protections. The states say Grok’s safeguards were weak or easily bypassed; SpaceX’s AI u
business.content: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX and related companies on Nov. 23, alleging that Grok’s AI image tools enabled users to create sexualized images of real people, including children, and that the company misled consumers about safety protections. The states say Grok’s safeguards were weak or easily bypassed; SpaceX’s AI unit, SpaceX Super Intelligence, says it blocks such requests, takes action against accounts and reports harmful content to law enforcement. The cases invoke state consumer-protection laws and seek court orders to stop the alleged conduct, civil penalties and other remedies; Virginia also seeks consumer restitution. Virginia seeks $2,500 for each alleged willful violation, with the number of violations to be determined at trial. The suits add to existing individual lawsuits and government investigations into Grok and X, SpaceX’s social platform.
business.image_alt: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok sexualized images

business.title: Amazon agrees to acquire Decart AI software in reported $7.5B deal
business.summary: Amazon agreed on Nov. 23 to acquire Israeli startup Decart’s AI optimization technology and hire its three co-founders and its research and engineering staff to improve the performance of its custom chips. Bloomberg reported a price of about $7.5 billion, but Amazon did not disclose financial terms; the transaction req
business.content: Amazon agreed on Nov. 23 to acquire Israeli startup Decart’s AI optimization technology and hire its three co-founders and its research and engineering staff to improve the performance of its custom chips. Bloomberg reported a price of about $7.5 billion, but Amazon did not disclose financial terms; the transaction requires regulatory clearance. Decart’s software helps AI models run across chips from Amazon, Nvidia and Google, and Amazon says it can help customers train and run models faster and at lower cost. Amazon plans to make its Trainium processors available outside its own cloud data centers in late 2027, CEO Andy Jassy said. Amazon is acquiring the technology behind Decart’s optimization platform, not its internally developed AI models. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory review.
business.image_alt: Amazon agrees to acquire Decart AI software in reported $7.5B deal

business.title: Democrats put Medicare expansion and universal coverage on 2027 agenda
business.summary: Democrats preparing to take control of Congress on Jan. 3, 2027, are prioritizing Medicare expansion and universal health coverage, with proposals to lower Medicare’s eligibility age and cover children. The agenda revives ideas long championed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, who is expected to lead the Senate health committee
business.content: Democrats preparing to take control of Congress on Jan. 3, 2027, are prioritizing Medicare expansion and universal health coverage, with proposals to lower Medicare’s eligibility age and cover children. The agenda revives ideas long championed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, who is expected to lead the Senate health committee and has proposed phasing in broader coverage over four years. Democrats say their early legislative work will include reversing Medicaid cuts and restoring tax credits for Affordable Care Act insurance plans. They also plan to add dental, vision and hearing benefits. The scope and financing remain unsettled: party members differ over incremental expansions versus a single-payer system, and Senate legislation could face a 60-vote hurdle as well as President Donald Trump’s veto.
business.image_alt: Democrats put Medicare expansion and universal coverage on 2027 agenda

science.title: Simulations point to possible second hidden planet beyond Neptune
science.summary: An international team led by Patryk Sofia Lykawka, an astrophysicist at Japan’s Kindai University, used computer simulations to propose that an undetected planet dubbed Planet X2 could help explain unusual orbits of icy bodies beyond Neptune. The best-fitting models give the planet one to two times Earth’s mass, a semi
science.content: An international team led by Patryk Sofia Lykawka, an astrophysicist at Japan’s Kindai University, used computer simulations to propose that an undetected planet dubbed Planet X2 could help explain unusual orbits of icy bodies beyond Neptune. The best-fitting models give the planet one to two times Earth’s mass, a semimajor axis of 350 to 500 astronomical units and a closest approach to the Sun of about 200 astronomical units. The simulations traced 4.5 billion years of Solar System evolution, including the migration of the giant planets. Planet X2 remains a hypothesis, not a discovery. The models reproduce several observed orbital patterns but do not fully match the distribution of objects’ orbital sizes. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile is surveying the sky. Its growing catalogue of distant objects will let astronomers test whether the predicted orbital patterns are more widespread. A direct sighting would be harder because the planet would be extremely faint.
science.image_alt: Simulations point to possible second hidden planet beyond Neptune

science.title: Researchers advance neutral-atom quantum computing
science.summary: Many experts believe neutral-atom technology could yield a usable quantum computer this decade. Companies and researchers are also pursuing superconducting processors and semiconductor systems. Hitachi is working toward a silicon-based processor, targeting 100 qubits in 2028 and 1,000 in 2030. Researchers still face ch
science.content: Many experts believe neutral-atom technology could yield a usable quantum computer this decade. Companies and researchers are also pursuing superconducting processors and semiconductor systems. Hitachi is working toward a silicon-based processor, targeting 100 qubits in 2028 and 1,000 in 2030. Researchers still face challenges in controlling errors and building larger, reliable machines.

science.title: Anthropic mathematician posts claimed AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis
science.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, posted what he described as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on Nov. 20, saying he developed it over six weeks with help from the company’s Claude AI system. The 1859 conjecture concerns the zeros of the Riemann zeta function and their connec
science.content: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, posted what he described as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on Nov. 20, saying he developed it over six weeks with help from the company’s Claude AI system. The 1859 conjecture concerns the zeros of the Riemann zeta function and their connection to the distribution of prime numbers. The proof is formalized in Lean, software that checks mathematical arguments. Its verification code contains more than 17 million lines, and a prose version reportedly exceeded 250,000 pages. Some mathematicians report independent checks, but others say the result is not yet fully confirmed, and researchers are still trying to understand the argument. If valid, the proof would affect many results that rely on the hypothesis.
science.image_alt: Anthropic mathematician posts claimed AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis

science.title: China plans 90 experiments and technology tests on Shenzhou-24 mission
science.summary: China’s Shenzhou-24 mission is scheduled to carry out 90 scientific experiments and technology tests aboard the Tiangong space station, including four joint China-Pakistan projects in biotechnology and materials science. Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will help install samples and equipment and condu
science.content: China’s Shenzhou-24 mission is scheduled to carry out 90 scientific experiments and technology tests aboard the Tiangong space station, including four joint China-Pakistan projects in biotechnology and materials science. Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will help install samples and equipment and conduct experiments during a short visit. The mission’s research spans space life sciences, materials, microgravity physics, medicine and new space technologies. The Shenzhou-24 crew, including Ali and Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, is due to launch from Jiuquan on Nov. 25. The spacecraft is expected to make an autonomous rapid rendezvous and dock at the forward port of Tiangong’s Tianhe core module. Zhu Yangzhu will remain aboard for a year-long in-orbit experiment to test long-duration spaceflight.
science.image_alt: China plans 90 experiments and technology tests on Shenzhou-24 mission

science.title: Milky Way study recasts part of Norma arm as star-forming bar shock
science.summary: A study published in *Nature Astronomy* suggests that a stretch of the Milky Way’s Norma arm traced by masers may instead be a star-forming shock front along the leading edge of the galaxy’s central bar. The University of Sydney-led team reached that interpretation by comparing galaxy simulations with existing maser me
science.content: A study published in *Nature Astronomy* suggests that a stretch of the Milky Way’s Norma arm traced by masers may instead be a star-forming shock front along the leading edge of the galaxy’s central bar. The University of Sydney-led team reached that interpretation by comparing galaxy simulations with existing maser measurements; it did not directly image the shock front or collect new observations. The researchers say the result concerns only the maser segment near the bar’s end, not the entire Norma-Outer arm, and requires further investigation.
science.image_alt: Milky Way study recasts part of Norma arm as star-forming bar shock

science.title: Voyager 1 reaches record distance of one light-day from Earth
science.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026, the farthest any human-made object has traveled. At about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers), a radio signal now takes 24 hours to travel one way between Earth and the probe. Voyager 1 continues to measure interstellar space, but i
science.content: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026, the farthest any human-made object has traveled. At about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers), a radio signal now takes 24 hours to travel one way between Earth and the probe. Voyager 1 continues to measure interstellar space, but its dwindling plutonium-powered electricity supply is forcing engineers to shut down equipment to conserve power. Its power output drops by about 4 watts a year, and the spacecraft could run out of power and go silent by 2036. A recent communications problem has also left engineers without science data to diagnose an onboard fault.
science.image_alt: Voyager 1 reaches record distance of one light-day from Earth

science.title: BepiColombo adjusts Mercury orbit plan after software glitch
science.summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) says it has revised BepiColombo’s remaining maneuvers after a software problem cut short the spacecraft’s Mercury orbit-insertion burn. The joint ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission to study Mercury remains in a stable orbit. The revised plan is expected to correct its tra
science.content: The European Space Agency (ESA) says it has revised BepiColombo’s remaining maneuvers after a software problem cut short the spacecraft’s Mercury orbit-insertion burn. The joint ESA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission to study Mercury remains in a stable orbit. The revised plan is expected to correct its trajectory without additional thruster burns. ESA’s analysis points to a software problem involving attitude and thruster control, though the precise cause remains under investigation. The revised sequence is intended to maintain the mission’s schedule: the orbiters are still due to separate in December, with routine science operations planned for April 2027.
science.image_alt: BepiColombo adjusts Mercury orbit plan after software glitch

science.title: November
science.summary: November’s Beaver Moon reached its full phase at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time Tuesday, Nov. 24, beginning a run of three consecutive supermoons, NASA says. The full moon was about 224,170 miles from Earth; NASA planetary scientist Noah Petro said it appeared about 17% larger and 30% brighter than the year’s smallest full moo
science.content: November’s Beaver Moon reached its full phase at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time Tuesday, Nov. 24, beginning a run of three consecutive supermoons, NASA says. The full moon was about 224,170 miles from Earth; NASA planetary scientist Noah Petro said it appeared about 17% larger and 30% brighter than the year’s smallest full moon. Because the peak occurred during daylight in North America, evening viewing offered the clearest chance to see it. A supermoon occurs when a full moon is near perigee, the moon’s closest point to Earth in its orbit. The size difference can be subtle to the eye, while the moon illusion can make the moon seem much larger when it is near the horizon. December’s Cold Moon is next, reaching its peak on Dec. 23.

sports.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis before Anthony Joshua heavyweight bout
sports.summary: Former unified heavyweight champion Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder after a psychiatric assessment in 2016. He publicly reveals the schizophrenia diagnosis in a Netflix documentary due for release on November 27. He describes a severe mental-health crisis after his 2015 win over
sports.content: Former unified heavyweight champion Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder after a psychiatric assessment in 2016. He publicly reveals the schizophrenia diagnosis in a Netflix documentary due for release on November 27. He describes a severe mental-health crisis after his 2015 win over Wladimir Klitschko, including hearing voices and struggling with alcohol and drugs. Fury was admitted to hospital in June 2016 after what he thought might be a heart attack. Doctors identified an anxiety attack, and he later saw a psychiatrist in London. He says the voices and anxiety left him unable to hold ordinary conversations, while his wife, Paris, recalls how frightened he seemed in hospital. Fury identifies Halloween night in 2017 as the point when he began turning his life around. He returned to boxing and beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to win another world title. After two losses to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024 and a retirement announcement, he returned with two wins in 2026. He is scheduled to fight fellow British heavyweight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11, with the bout also set to stream on Netflix.
sports.image_alt: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis before Anthony Joshua heavyweight bout

sports.title: PSG face January decision after ACL injuries sideline two wingers
sports.summary: Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) forward Désiré Doué has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee and is expected to miss most or all of the season after suffering the injury in Saturday’s 3-2 win at Nice. His absence follows a similar injury to winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in October, leaving PSG witho
sports.content: Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) forward Désiré Doué has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee and is expected to miss most or all of the season after suffering the injury in Saturday’s 3-2 win at Nice. His absence follows a similar injury to winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in October, leaving PSG without two major attacking options as they seek a third consecutive Champions League title. PSG have not decided whether to sign a forward in January or rely on their current squad. Manager Luis Enrique says the club is open to signings but believes the squad can cope. PSG won their first four Champions League league-phase matches and led the 36-team table at the halfway point. Doué is expected to undergo surgery, while PSG will assess their remaining attacking options before the winter transfer window.

sports.content: Max Verstappen won Saturday’s Las Vegas Grand Prix for Red Bull, beating McLaren’s Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds, with Norris’s teammate Oscar Piastri third. The lead changed repeatedly, with several drivers in contention for victory. Mercedes’ George Russell, who had battled Verstappen for the lead, locked up late and finished ninth. After a practice clash with Russell, Verstappen mocked his rival’s late error. Russell said he had taken the risk because he was going for the win. Verstappen also criticized the racing’s reliance on battery power and overtake mode, saying it was not the Formula One he wanted to see. Formula One next heads to Qatar, followed by the Abu Dhabi season finale on December 6.

sports.content: England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, FIFA confirmed on November 23 after approving the unopposed bid by acclamation. It will be the first World Cup staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament. The same FIFA Congress confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as hosts of the 2031 edition, when the women’s tournament expands to 48 teams for the first time. The 2035 competition is planned for 48 teams, 104 matches and 39 days. The UK bid initially proposed 19 venues, while three additional stadium projects could expand the candidate list; FIFA will ultimately select 14 to 16 grounds. FIFA’s evaluation scored the bid 4.3 out of five but identified unresolved questions over government guarantees, including tax arrangements. The four football associations and UK governments have more than eight years to prepare, including selecting and upgrading venues. The government wants one million more girls to play, watch or hold leadership roles in sport by 2035. Officials are still discussing affordable ticketing and FIFA’s tax-related demands.

Gill said the ball became soft after about 2
sports.content: India captain Shubman Gill has called on the International Cricket Council (ICC), cricket’s governing body, to reverse its saliva ban after New Zealand batted out a draw in the first Test in Wellington, where India’s bowlers could not take the final five wickets they needed. Gill said the ball became soft after about 25 to 30 overs, making it harder to create chances on a pitch that offered little help. New Zealand captain Tom Latham agreed the ball softened during the match but was unsure whether the saliva rule should change, saying teams must adapt to current playing conditions. The ban was introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic and made permanent in 2022; players may still use sweat to shine the ball. Gill also questioned whether Kookaburra balls retain their hardness, citing similar concerns about the Dukes ball during India’s 2025 tour of England. Gill said he left fast bowler Mohammed Siraj out because of his form, while former India players Subramaniam Badrinath and Aakash Chopra argued the experienced seamer should have played. India and New Zealand meet again in Christchurch on November 27, with the series still undecided.

sports.content: The ATP’s final 2026 rankings place Alexander Zverev first, Jannik Sinner second and Carlos Alcaraz third, after Alcaraz beat Zverev in Sunday’s ATP Finals championship match. Zverev finished with 10,350 points, ahead of Sinner’s 7,950 and Alcaraz’s 7,600. Alcaraz’s unbeaten run to the Turin title narrowed his deficit to Sinner to 350 points. The year-end No. 1 ranking is a first for Zverev and for a German man. At 29 years and 217 days, he is the oldest player to earn the year-end honor for the first time, slightly older than Andre Agassi was when he first achieved it in 1999. Alcaraz, 23, finished a season in which he completed the career Grand Slam and returned from a wrist injury that kept him out for more than four months. Both finalists will next play in the Davis Cup Final 8 in Bologna, which runs through Nov. 29. Spain is scheduled to face Austria and Germany to play Great Britain in the quarterfinals on Thursday, Nov. 26.

Metcalf denied trying to poke De
sports.content: The NFL will not suspend Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after his ejection against the Philadelphia Eagles for two personal fouls, including an apparent reach toward Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean’s facemask; the league is still reviewing the incident for a possible fine. Metcalf denied trying to poke DeJean in the eye and said he was telling him to “stop pushing me”. Metcalf is eligible for Pittsburgh’s Friday home game against the Denver Broncos, though he could still face a fine. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy initially called the ejection unacceptable, then said his Monday conversation with Metcalf was productive and that he appreciated how the receiver communicated. Metcalf said he wished he had stayed on the field to help his teammates. Metcalf had one catch for two yards before leaving Sunday’s 19-16 loss, Pittsburgh’s second straight defeat; the Steelers are 6-4. Pittsburgh’s next three games are against Denver, Jacksonville and Houston, and the Steelers remain in playoff position.

sports.content: Manchester United’s new head coach Mauricio Pochettino began his tenure with a 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on Nov. 22, leaving the club 19th with eight points after 11 Premier League games; defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. United have conceded 34 goals in all competitions, while striker Benjamin Sesko is sidelined by a shin injury. Pochettino and the club’s board have reportedly made signing a striker their January priority, but his expected budget is below £50 million. United plan only two additions, possibly including a loan, under Premier League financial rules. United focused on midfield in the summer and did not bring in a new striker or left-back. Pochettino is expected to discuss winter recruitment with club chiefs this week. His next match is away to Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, Nov. 25.
